description:
October 2026 marked a strong beginning to Fiscal Year 2027 for the City of Greenacres Economic Development Department. Building upon the prior fiscal year’s accomplishments, the Department continued advancing business attraction and retention, redevelopment, workforce development, entrepreneurship, regional collaboration, and expanded economic opportunities.
During the month, the Department strengthened partnerships with public- and private-sector organizations, supported business development and procurement opportunities, celebrated entrepreneurs, connected employers with prospective employees, and promoted Greenacres’ economic development initiatives nationally.
1. Strategic Partnerships And Regional Collaboration20th Annual Palm Beach Partners Business MatchMaker Conference & ExpoOn October 2, 2026, the City participated as a regional partner in the 20th Annual Palm Beach Partners Business MatchMaker Conference & Expo, themed “Building Bridges • Creating Futures.” The conference connected entrepreneurs, small businesses, public agencies, procurement professionals, educational institutions, and private-sector organizations. The program included educational workshops, networking, and one-on-one PowerTalk sessions. Dimension 20, Forest Hill High School’s award-winning choral group directed by Sterling Frederick, opened the conference, and Perla Tamez Casasnovas, CEO of Casasnovas Capital, delivered the luncheon keynote. Through Palm Beach Partners, the City supports opportunities for small businesses to pursue public- and private-sector contracts, expand professional networks, and access resources for sustainable growth.
Recognition of Greenacres Business PartnersProfessional Services Excellence Award Honoree – Kaliah Communications, Inc. The City nominated Kaliah Communications, led by Michelle Brown, for its creative and strategic work on “Dine Local. Savor Greenacres.” The nomination cited nearly 50,000 combined social media views and business participation interest increasing by more than 200%, demonstrating the potential of storytelling and digital promotion to strengthen local business visibility.
Pioneer Progress Award Honoree – Designs To Go. The City recognized Cesar A. Sanchez and Designs To Go for more than 25 years of partnership, including City events, public-space enhancements, and creative installations. During the Centennial, the business donated vinyl wrapping materials to help celebrate Greenacres’ history and identity through public art.
Hispanic Heritage Month Business Networking MixerOn October 14, the City partnered with Palm Beach County’s Department of Housing and Economic Development to host a Hispanic Heritage Month Networking Mixer at CocoCabana Bar & Grill, 2944 South Jog Road. The event celebrated Hispanic-owned businesses and fostered connections among entrepreneurs, business leaders, and community partners.
Heritage Chamber of Commerce – Anniversary and Business Excellence Awards
On October 16, the Department participated in the Heritage Chamber of Commerce’s “Symphony of Cultures” Anniversary and Business Excellence Awards celebration. The event recognized regional entrepreneurial achievement. The Economic Development Director’s appointment to the Chamber’s Advisory Board further expands opportunities to connect Greenacres businesses with regional resources and networks.
2. Workforce Development and Employment Opportunities5th Annual The Palm Beaches Hospitality & Tourism Job FairOn October 9, 2026, the City, in partnership with Discover The Palm Beaches and CareerSource Palm Beach County, hosted the 5th Annual The Palm Beaches Hospitality & Tourism Job Fair. The event brought together 23 employers and 201 job applicants, providing direct access to hiring representatives and career opportunities in hospitality and tourism.
Participating employers represented hotels, restaurants, attractions, and related services. The event helped employers promote openings and strengthen recruitment pipelines while connecting job seekers with potential career pathways. The Department will continue working with partners to evaluate hiring outcomes.
3. Economic Development Leadership and International Visibility2026 International City/County Management Association Annual ConferenceDuring October, Dr. Philip C. Harris represented Greenacres at the 2026 ICMA Annual Conference, participating in two presentations on local government and economic development best practices before a professional audience drawn from approximately 5,000 conference participants. The engagement elevated awareness of Greenacres’ initiatives and provided opportunities to exchange strategies with municipal leaders.
4. Business Assistance And EntrepreneurshipSCORE Business MentoringThe Department continued its partnership with SCORE, offering confidential, one-on-one business mentoring at City Hall on the third Thursday of each month. Volunteer professionals provide guidance on startup planning, financial management, marketing, expansion, and business operations.
Supporting Small Business Visibility and GrowthThe Department continued supporting locally owned businesses through outreach and digital promotion. “Dine Local. Savor Greenacres.” and “Buy Local. Shop Greenacres.” reinforce the City’s role as a marketing partner, encourage local spending, and celebrate the businesses that contribute to the community’s distinctive identity.
5. Redevelopment And Investment OutreachStrategic Corridor Redevelopment and Hotel InvestmentThroughout October, the Department engaged developers, property owners, hospitality representatives, and investors regarding redevelopment opportunities along Lake Worth Road, 10th Avenue North, Haverhill Road, and Jog Road. Discussions included potential Hilton-affiliated and Cobblestone hotel development interests, as well as mixed-use, multifamily, retail, workforce housing, and underutilized commercial property opportunities.
Expand and diversify the municipal tax base.
Encourage private-sector investment and revitalization of underutilized properties.
Create commercial activity and employment opportunities.
Expand hospitality and visitor-serving amenities.
Strengthen the competitiveness of Greenacres’ commercial corridors.
The Department will continue facilitating connections between property owners and prospective investors while advancing opportunities consistent with the City’s long-term redevelopment vision.
6. FY 2027 Strategic PrioritiesBuilding upon the momentum of the prior fiscal year, the Department will focus on the following interconnected priorities:
Redevelopment and Investment Attraction: Advance hotel opportunities, mixed-use redevelopment, and commercial corridor investment.
Business Retention and Expansion: Strengthen relationships with existing businesses and provide access to growth resources.
Entrepreneurship and Business Assistance: Expand mentoring, technical assistance, procurement access, and business education.
Workforce Development: Connect employers and residents through targeted job fairs and career pathways.
Education and Future Workforce Readiness: Expand Greenacres Grows Scholars and school-business partnerships.
Regional and International Partnerships: Build relationships that expand opportunity and visibility.
Performance and Accountability: Document outcomes and communicate the measurable impact of City initiatives.
CONCLUSIONOctober 2026 demonstrated a strong and productive beginning to FY 2027. Through regional business partnerships, workforce recruitment, national professional engagement, entrepreneurial assistance, and continued redevelopment outreach, the Department remains focused on translating strategic relationships into economic opportunities.
As Greenacres celebrates its Centennial Year, the Department remains dedicated to advancing sustainable growth, attracting investment, strengthening business partnerships, and enhancing quality of life.

description:
Executive Summary
This report, prepared by the Communications and Governmental Affairs Department, is submitted in accordance with Section 9-12 of the Code of the City of Greenacres, which requires that the City Mayor or City Mayor's designee comply with the reporting requirements established in Section 316.0776(3)(c), Florida Statutes. Pursuant to that requirement, each jurisdiction that operates one or more school zone speed detection systems must annually report the results of all systems within its jurisdiction by placing the report as a single item on the agenda of a regular or special meeting of the respective governing body. The item must allow for public comment and may not be considered as part of the consent agenda.
The information provided in this report covers the period from July 1, 2025, through the end of the school year on June 30, 2026. No systems were activated during summer school. During this period, four speed detection systems were installed across two school zones, and a total of 130 Notices of Violation (NOVs) were issued.
Background
During the 2023 State Legislative Session, the Florida Legislature enacted House Bill 657 and Senate Bill 766, codified in part at Sections 316.003, 316.008, 316.0776 and 316.1896, Florida Statutes. These provisions authorize counties or municipalities to deploy automated speed detection systems in school zones to enforce speed limits, subject to specified requirements for implementation, administration, and due process.
On May 19, 2025, the Greenacres City Council adopted Ordinance 2025-02, authorizing the installation of speed detection systems to enforce applicable speed limits in school zones within incorporated City of Greenacres. The ordinance identified 12 school zones for future installation. Ordinance No. 2025-02
Subsequently, on January 6, 2026, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 2026-30, approving an agreement with American Traffic Solutions, Inc., d.b.a. (Verra Mobility) to provide a turnkey solution for the purchase, installation, operation and maintenance of automated speed detection and enforcement systems in City school zones. Under the agreement, Verra Mobility is also responsible for billing, collection, distribution of violation proceeds, and completion of quarterly reports required by the Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles on behalf of the County.
Two school zones, comprising of four detection systems, were activated at the beginning of the program in January 6, 2026. By the end of the 2025-26 school year, a total of four detection systems across two school zones were fully operational.
Statutory Reporting Requirements
Section 316.0776(3)(c), Florida Statutes, requires that a municipality operating speed detection systems annually submit a report to its governing body detailing the results of all such systems. The report must contain: (1) the number of NOVs issued; (2) the number of NOVs contested; (3) the number of NOVs upheld; (4) the number of NOVs dismissed; (5) the number of NOVs issued as uniform traffic citations; (6) the number of NOVs paid; and (7) the distribution and amount of collected funds.
Section 316.1896(5), Florida Statutes, prescribes the allocation of funds derived from the program. Of each penalty collected, the municipality retains $60 per violation to administer the program and support other public safety initiatives, while the remaining $40 is remitted and distributed as follows: (1) $20 to the Department of Revenue for deposit into the General Revenue Fund; (2) $12 to the School District for school security, student transportation or pedestrian safety improvements; (3) $5 to the County or municipality for the School Guard Recruitment and Retention Program; and (4) $3 to the Department of Revenue for deposit into the Department of Law Enforcement Criminal Justice Standards and Training Trust Fund.
Pursuant to the Cities agreement, Verra Mobility receives a share of the $60 retained by the City, i.e., 32 percent for Program Revenue from the cameras installed.

Conclusion
This report fulfills the annual reporting requirement under Section 316.0776(3)(c), Florida Statutes, and Section 9-12, of the City Code, demonstrating compliance with the Florida School Zone Speed Detection Program’s statutory and administrative provisions. description:
Florida Statutes Section 200.065 specifies the procedural steps that must be followed by each unit of local government in the preparation and approval of the government entity's property tax millage, levy, and annual budget. description:
BACKGROUND
August 2026 represented another month of significant progress and positive momentum for the City of Greenacres’ economic development efforts. The Economic Development Department continued advancing strategic priorities focused on redevelopment and investment attraction, small business growth, workforce development, educational partnerships, business visibility, and regional collaboration.
During the month, the Department advanced discussions with developers and hospitality investors, expanded the Greenacres Grows Scholars Initiative, supported new and existing businesses, strengthened entrepreneurial assistance, successfully hosted a skilled-trades workforce event, and continued building partnerships that connect residents and businesses with economic opportunities.
As Greenacres celebrates its Centennial Year, these accomplishments demonstrate how strategic relationships are being transformed into tangible opportunities. The Department remains focused on positioning Greenacres as a competitive, business-friendly community where investment is welcomed, entrepreneurs are supported, residents are connected to opportunity, and partnerships produce meaningful results.
1. REDEVELOPMENT AND INVESTMENT OUTREACH
Corridor Redevelopment and Hotel Investment
Throughout August, the Department continued strategic discussions with developers, property owners, investors, and hospitality representatives regarding redevelopment opportunities along the Lake Worth Road commercial corridor.
Particular emphasis remained on advancing potential hotel investment opportunities, including discussions involving Hilton-affiliated development interests and Cobblestone Hotels. The Department continues identifying potential sites, connecting property owners with prospective investors and developers, and positioning Greenacres for additional hospitality investment.
Discussions also continued regarding mixed-use, multifamily residential, retail, and workforce housing opportunities that complement the City’s long-term redevelopment vision.• Expanding and diversifying the municipal tax base;
• Encouraging redevelopment of underutilized commercial properties;
• Attracting new private-sector investment;
• Creating employment opportunities;
• Expanding hospitality and visitor-serving amenities; and
• Strengthening the long-term economic vitality of the Lake Worth Road corridor.
The sustained engagement of developers, property owners, and investors reflects growing market confidence in Greenacres and demonstrates the value of the City’s proactive approach to investment attraction and redevelopment.
2. GREENACRES GROWS SCHOLARS INITIATIVE
The newly established Greenacres Grows Scholars Initiative continued gaining significant support from the local business and community sectors during August.
To date, 15 business and community partners have committed to supporting Greenacres students and schools through one or more components of the initiative.
Greenacres Grows Scholars is structured around three primary pillars:• Adopt-A-School Business Partnerships – Connecting businesses directly with Greenacres-area schools to provide resources, engagement, mentoring, and other forms of support.
• Attendance Matters Recognition – Engaging businesses as sponsors to recognize and encourage students who demonstrate excellent or improved school attendance.
• Greenacres Future Leaders Scholarship Fund – Creating a business-supported scholarship resource to help Greenacres students pursue postsecondary education and career opportunities.
The initiative also provides opportunities for businesses to participate through mentoring, career speakers, job shadowing, business tours, internships, and workforce-readiness activities.
Early Partnership Results• 15 Business and Community Partners
• 9 Attendance Recognition Sponsors
• 6 Scholarship Fund Partners
• 5 Adopt-A-School Partners
• 5 Mentor Program Partners
• 5 Career Speaker Partners
• 1 Job Shadowing Host
• 1 Business Tour Host
These figures represent partnership commitments rather than unique businesses, as several partners have committed to supporting multiple components of the initiative.
Attendance Matters currently has the strongest level of participation, providing an important foundation for connecting businesses with schools to recognize students for outstanding or improved attendance. The scholarship component has also generated strong early interest, while commitments to mentoring and career presentations will allow participating businesses to establish meaningful relationships with students beyond financial contributions.
Business partners have expressed interest in supporting several Greenacres-area schools, including Greenacres Elementary, Cholee Lake Elementary, Diamond View Elementary, Heritage Elementary, Liberty Park Elementary, Greenacres Christian Academy, Montessori Academy of Early Enrichment, and Potentia Academy.
The next phase will focus on converting these commitments into active school-business partnerships by confirming participating schools and liaisons, matching businesses with schools, coordinating Attendance Matters activities, establishing scholarship commitments, and developing mentoring and career-exposure opportunities.
The initiative represents an important connection between economic development, education, and workforce development. By engaging the business community in the development of Greenacres students today, the City is helping strengthen the workforce and community leadership pipeline of tomorrow.
3. BUSINESS ASSISTANCE, ENTREPRENEURSHIP, AND BUSINESS VISIBILITY
Buy Local. Shop Greenacres. – Quince Gallery
During August, the Department continued its “Buy Local. Shop Greenacres” digital business spotlight initiative with its second featured business, Quince Gallery, located at 3086 Jog Road.
Building upon the success of the City’s award-winning “Dine Local. Savor Greenacres" campaign, “Buy Local. Shop Greenacres” expands the City’s digital marketing support to locally owned retailers and service businesses.
Through professional storytelling and the City’s communications platforms, the initiative provides participating businesses with promotional exposure at no cost while encouraging residents and visitors to discover businesses that contribute to the unique “Only in Greenacres” experience.
This initiative represents the City’s evolving role as not only a facilitator of economic development but also a strategic marketing partner for the local business community.
Ribbon Cutting & 4th Anniversary – PPEC of Palm Beach
On August 14, 2026, City leadership and staff joined PPEC of Palm Beach to celebrate its ribbon cutting and fourth anniversary.
PPEC of Palm Beach provides specialized medical daycare services for medically fragile children under the age of 21. The organization integrates skilled nursing care, therapeutic support, educational enrichment, recreation, and family resources within a safe and nurturing environment.
The organization’s continued presence in Greenacres adds to the City’s growing healthcare and family-service economy while providing an important resource for children and families throughout the community.
Grand Opening & Ribbon Cutting – Spirit Halloween
On August 19, 2026, City leadership and staff participated in the grand opening and ribbon-cutting celebration for Spirit Halloween at RiverBridge Plaza.
Spirit Halloween operates more than 1,450 seasonal locations across North America and is recognized as a leading seasonal retailer for costumes, décor, accessories, and Halloween merchandise.
The Greenacres location provides another example of productive commercial-space activation. Seasonal retailers can generate customer traffic, create temporary employment opportunities, and bring renewed activity to available commercial space.
The City welcomed Spirit Halloween to Greenacres and was pleased to support its investment in the local commercial community.
Grand Opening & Ribbon Cutting – Los Compadres Barbershop
On August 20, 2026, City leadership and staff celebrated the official ribbon cutting for Los Compadres Barbershop.
Los Compadres has developed a strong reputation for professional barbering services and customer service. More importantly, the owners have demonstrated a commitment to building relationships, supporting the community, and making a long-term investment in Greenacres.
Small businesses such as Los Compadres contribute significantly to the character and vitality of the City’s commercial corridors and represent the entrepreneurial spirit that the Department remains committed to supporting.
Florida State University – WPEAP Community Bootcamp
During August, the West Palm Entrepreneurship and Adversity Program (WPEAP) began its third Community Bootcamp for Entrepreneurs at the Florida State University West Palm Collaboration Space.
The City of Greenacres is proud to serve as a community partner for this initiative through the Jim Moran Institute for Global Entrepreneurship.
The program supports individuals seeking to start or grow businesses while navigating economic or other barriers. Participants receive practical business education, mentorship, professional connections, and access to resources designed to help transform business ideas into sustainable enterprises.
This partnership reflects the Department’s broader philosophy that economic development extends beyond attracting new investment. A strong local economy also requires ensuring that existing businesses, entrepreneurs, and aspiring business owners have access to the knowledge, relationships, and resources necessary to succeed.
Prospera – Bilingual Business Technical Assistance
The Department continued its partnership with Prospera through monthly Pop-Up Business Consultations at City Hall.
These bilingual consultations provide entrepreneurs and business owners with individualized assistance related to business management, access to capital, planning, marketing, and other areas necessary for business growth.
Year-to-date results demonstrate the measurable impact of this partnership:• 43 clients received consulting assistance;
• 37 clients were existing business owners;
• 38 jobs were created or retained;
• 8 clients received specialized Business Advancement Services; and
• 60+ participants received education through orientations, seminars, and workshops.
These results demonstrate how strategic partnerships can translate directly into business assistance, employment impact, and stronger local enterprises.
SCORE Business Mentoring
The Department continued its partnership with SCORE, providing confidential one-on-one business mentoring at City Hall on the third Thursday of each month.
SCORE’s volunteer professionals provide entrepreneurs and existing businesses with guidance related to startup planning, business strategy, financial management, expansion, and operational challenges.
Together, Prospera, SCORE, WPEAP, and the City’s business marketing initiatives provide entrepreneurs with a continuum of support, from developing a business idea to strengthening, expanding, and promoting an established enterprise.
4. COLLABORATION, PARTNERSHIP, AND COMMUNITY RECOGNITION
City of Greenacres Wins People’s Choice Award
During August, the City of Greenacres earned First Place in the Government category of the Black Chamber of Commerce of Palm Beach County’s 2026 Our People’s Choice Awards.
The recognition celebrates the City’s creativity, tenacity, commitment to excellence, and positive impact within Palm Beach County.
This award reflects the collective efforts of the Mayor and City Council, City Administration, employees, residents, businesses, and community partners who continue working together to make Greenacres a welcoming, innovative, and thriving community.
The celebration was made even more meaningful by the recognition of PostNet Palm Beach, a Greenacres small business that also earned First Place in its respective category.
These recognitions provide positive visibility for both the City and its local business community and demonstrate what is possible when government, businesses, residents, and community organizations work together toward shared success.
5. WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT
NextUp Skilled Trades: Speed Networking & Career Connection
August marked a major workforce-development accomplishment with the successful NextUp Skilled Trades: Speed Networking & Career Connection event.
The event welcomed approximately 130 attendees and 20 participating businesses, industry professionals, and mentors for an evening focused on connecting the next generation with career opportunities in construction, skilled trades, engineering, architecture, design, and related industries.
Students and young adults were able to engage directly with professionals, ask questions, explore career pathways, establish professional connections, and gain exposure to industries that are helping build and shape communities throughout South Florida.
The event demonstrated workforce development at the local level by bringing together education, business, government, industry, and community partners to connect residents with real career pathways and help employers strengthen their future talent pipeline.
The Department appreciates the partnership of the NKBA Treasure Coast Chapter, PBC Design & Trades Networking Mixer, participating businesses, mentors, students, parents, and community partners whose involvement contributed to the event’s success.
Meet industry professionals. Explore career pathways. Build your future.
Essential Trades Career Fair – September 23
Building upon this workforce momentum, the Department continued preparations for the Essential Trades Career Fair, scheduled for September 23, 2026.
The City is partnering with National Remodelers Charities, CareerSource Palm Beach County, Express Employment Professionals, and other community partners to connect students, job seekers, and emerging professionals with employers and career opportunities within the skilled trades.
The initiative will provide another direct pathway for residents to connect with employers, learn about in-demand occupations, and access resources that support employment and career advancement.
20th Annual Palm Beach Partners Business MatchMaker Conference & Expo
The Department also continued preparations for the 20th Annual Palm Beach Partners Business MatchMaker Conference & Expo.
The City of Greenacres is a partner in Palm Beach Partners, a collaborative network of public agencies, educational institutions, local governments, and economic development organizations working to increase opportunities for small and diverse businesses throughout Palm Beach County.
The conference will connect entrepreneurs, small businesses owners, and established companies directly with government agencies, corporations, procurement professionals, and prime contractors.
Under the theme “Building Bridges • Creating Futures,” the conference will provide opportunities for businesses to pursue government contracts, establish relationships with purchasing decision-makers, learn about upcoming procurement opportunities, and access educational resources related to financing, certifications, marketing, and business growth.

August 2026 demonstrated strong and measurable economic development momentum for the City of Greenacres. The Department continued advancing redevelopment and hotel investment discussions while simultaneously strengthening the foundations of the local economy through small business assistance, educational partnerships, workforce development, business attraction, and community engagement.
Importantly, several initiatives are now producing measurable outcomes: 15 businesses and community organizations have committed to Greenacres Grows Scholars; Prospera-supported activities have contributed to 38 jobs created or retained; approximately 130 participants engaged in the NextUp workforce initiative; new businesses and commercial activities continue to invest in Greenacres; and the City received countywide recognition through the 2026 People’s Choice Award.
These accomplishments demonstrate a comprehensive approach to economic development, attracting investment, supporting businesses, developing talent, strengthening partnerships, and investing in the next generation.
As Greenacres celebrates its Centennial Year, the Economic Development Department remains committed to building upon this momentum and translating relationships into opportunities, opportunities into investment, and investment into lasting economic prosperity.
A Century of Growth is not only a celebration of how far Greenacres has come, but it also reflects the momentum we are creating today and our commitment to building an even stronger economic future for the next 100 years.

description:
July 2026 represented another month of strong progress for the City of Greenacres' economic development efforts. The Economic Development Department continued advancing strategic priorities focused on redevelopment and investment attraction, small business development, workforce readiness, regional and international partnerships, and expanded opportunities for residents and entrepreneurs.
During the month, the Department continued engaging developers and hospitality investors, successfully facilitated the Mexican Mobile Consulate in Greenacres, expanded entrepreneurial education and technical assistance, strengthened partnerships with the business community, and advanced workforce development programming.
As Greenacres celebrates its Centennial Year, these initiatives reflect the City's continued transformation into a more connected, competitive, and business-friendly community. Through intentional partnerships and proactive economic development strategies, Greenacres continues building momentum toward sustainable investment, job creation, business growth, and an enhanced quality of life.
1. REDEVELOPMENT AND INVESTMENT OUTREACH
Corridor Redevelopment and Hotel Investment
Throughout July, the Department continued strategic discussions with developers, property owners, investors, and hospitality representatives regarding redevelopment opportunities along the Lake Worth Road commercial corridor.
Particular emphasis was placed on advancing potential hotel investment opportunities, including discussions involving Hilton affiliated development interests and Cobblestone Hotels. The Department continues working to identify appropriate sites, connect property owners with prospective investors, and position Greenacres for additional hospitality investment.
In addition to hotel development, discussions continued regarding mixed-use, multifamily residential, retail, and workforce housing opportunities that complement the City's long-term redevelopment vision.
These efforts support several important City objectives, including:
Expanding and differentiating the municipal tax base;
Encouraging redevelopment of underutilized commercial properties;
Attracting new private-sector investment;
Creating employment opportunities;
Expanding hospitality and visitor-serving amenities; and
Strengthening the long-term economic vitality of the Lake Worth Road corridor.
The continued engagement of developers and investors demonstrates growing confidence in the Greenacres market and reflects the City's proactive approach to creating an environment where quality development and investment can move forward.
2. STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT
Mexican Consulate of Miami – Mobile Consulate Initiative
On July 11, 2026, the City of Greenacres successfully hosted the Mexican Mobile Consulate at the Greenacres Community Center in partnership with the Consulate General of Mexico in Miami.
The initiative brought essential consular and community services directly to Greenacres and surrounding communities, reducing the need for residents to travel to the Consulate's headquarters in Miami-Dade County.
Services and resources included:
Passports and consular identification services;
Voter registration assistance;
Civil registry and dual-nationality resources;
Legal and immigration information;
Health and wellness resources;
Financial education; and
Community outreach and resource connections.
The initiative extended beyond traditional consular services. Through collaboration with Prospera, bilingual economic development resources were made available to connect entrepreneurs and residents with information related to access to capital, entrepreneurship, business planning, marketing, employment opportunities, and small business technical assistance.
Following the event, the Consulate General of Mexico in Miami formally recognized the City of Greenacres for its collaboration and support. In correspondence dated July 17, 2026, Consul General Rutilio Escandón Cadenas expressed gratitude to Mayor Charles Shaw and the City for providing the Greenacres Community Center and noted that the City's collaboration was essential to successfully bringing consular services closer to the Mexican community in Greenacres and surrounding areas.
The Consul General also specifically recognized the professionalism and commitment of the City's Economic Development Department and staff in facilitating the partnership and serving as an institutional liaison between Greenacres and the Consulate.
This successful initiative demonstrates the City's ability to leverage international and community partnerships to improve access to services while simultaneously creating pathways to entrepreneurship and economic opportunity.
3. BUSINESS ASSISTANCE, ENTREPRENEURSHIP, AND BUSINESS VISIBILITY
Buy Local. Shop Greenacres. – New Business Spotlight Initiative
In July, the Economic Development Department officially launched the City's first "Buy Local. Shop Greenacres." business spotlight, expanding Greenacres' innovative digital marketing efforts to support and promote locally owned retailers and service-based businesses.
Building upon the success of the award-winning "Dine Local. Savor Greenacres." campaign, Buy Local. Shop Greenacres is a new digital media series designed to showcase the small businesses that contribute to Greenacres' unique character and economy. From salons and boutiques to entertainment venues, barbershops, and other locally owned establishments, the initiative provides participating businesses with professional promotional exposure at no cost.
The campaign supports the City's broader economic development objectives by:
Increasing visibility for locally owned businesses;
Encouraging residents and visitors to spend locally;
Strengthening the City's small business ecosystem;
Promoting businesses and experiences that are unique to Greenacres;
Expanding the City's digital reach; and
Reinforcing Greenacres' distinctive "Only in Greenacres" identity.
The inaugural spotlight featured VYDA Salon & Spa, located at 2182 South Jog Road. Owner Gissela Tafur and her team provide a variety of beauty, wellness, and self-care services to the Greenacres community.
The launch represents another important evolution in the City's approach to economic development, using creative digital storytelling and the City's communications platforms to become an active marketing partner for local businesses.
New Business Grand Opening – Pho Hoa
On July 17, 2026, City leadership and staff participated in the official ribbon-cutting ceremony welcoming Pho Hoa to Greenacres at Riverbridge Plaza, 6716 Forest Hill Boulevard.
Pho Hoa brings an internationally recognized Vietnamese dining concept to the City's growing and culturally diverse restaurant community. The restaurant specializes in authentic Vietnamese pho prepared with fresh ingredients and traditional recipes. The name "Hòa," meaning "harmony," reflects the restaurant's philosophy of balancing tradition and innovation, flavor and nutrition, and Vietnamese culture.
The opening of Pho Hoa represents another positive addition to Greenacres' commercial landscape and further expands the dining experiences available to residents and visitors.
The City congratulates the Pho Hoa team on its investment in Greenacres and welcomes the restaurant to our growing business community.
Florida State University Jim Moran Institute Small Business Bootcamp
The Department continued promoting a new entrepreneurial development opportunity in partnership with the Jim Moran Institute for Global Entrepreneurship at Florida State University.
Applications were promoted for the West Palm Entrepreneurship and Adversity Program (WPEAP), an intensive six-week Community Bootcamp scheduled to begin August 15, 2026.
The program is designed to assist aspiring entrepreneurs and existing small business owners seeking to launch, stabilize, or grow their businesses. Participants will receive practical instruction and resources related to:
Entrepreneurship;
Marketing;
Financial management;
Business operations;
Strategic planning;
Mentoring and consulting; and
Community business resources.
Connecting Greenacres entrepreneurs with high-quality educational and technical resources strengthens the City's entrepreneurial pipeline and supports the long-term sustainability of locally owned businesses.
Prospera – Digital Presence to Increase Sales Seminar
During July, the Department partnered with Prospera to host a business development seminar focused on "Digital Presence to Increase Sales."
The seminar provided entrepreneurs and small business owners with practical guidance on marketing strategies, digital tools, artificial intelligence, customer engagement, and techniques for increasing their online visibility.
Participants were also able to ask questions, exchange ideas, network with fellow entrepreneurs, and establish connections with business-development professionals.
The strong participation demonstrated the entrepreneurial energy that continues to grow within Greenacres. Through partnerships such as Prospera, the City continues providing accessible and responsive resources designed to help businesses start, grow, and succeed.
SCORE Business Mentoring
The Department continued its partnership with SCORE, providing confidential one-on-one business mentoring sessions at City Hall on the third Thursday of each month.
SCORE's volunteer business professionals provide entrepreneurs and existing business owners with expertise related to startup planning, business strategy, expansion, financial management, and operational challenges.
Together, the City's partnerships with SCORE, Prospera, and the Jim Moran Institute provide entrepreneurs with a continuum of assistance, from developing an initial business concept to strengthening and expanding an established enterprise.
4. BUSINESS RETENTION, EXPANSION, AND COLLABORATION
Open for Business: City Leaders Roundtable
On July 30, 2026, the City partnered with the Black Chamber of Commerce of Palm Beach County to host Open for Business: City Leaders Roundtable at the Greenacres Community Center.
The event brought together municipal leaders, procurement professionals, business owners, entrepreneurs, and community partners to strengthen connections between local government and the business community.
The roundtable provided businesses with valuable information regarding:
Municipal procurement and contracting;
Vendor registration;
Certification opportunities;
Public-sector purchasing processes;
Upcoming projects and contracting opportunities;
Business development resources; and
Direct connections with municipal representatives.
The partnership created an important forum for moving beyond traditional networking toward meaningful connections, access to information, and expanded economic opportunities.
The City values its continued collaboration with the Black Chamber of Commerce of Palm Beach County and remains committed to ensuring that small businesses and entrepreneurs have greater awareness of and access to opportunities within local government.
5. Workforce Development
NextUp Skilled Trades: Speed Networking & Career Connection
During July, the Department continued planning for the NextUp Skilled Trades: Speed Networking & Career Connection Event, scheduled for August 26, 2026, at the Greenacres Community Center.
The initiative is being developed in partnership with PBC Design & Trades Networking Mixer and the National Kitchen & Bath Association's Treasure Coast Chapter to connect students, job seekers, and adults considering career changes with professionals from the construction, skilled trades, architecture, engineering, and design industries.
The event is designed to expose participants to career pathways that offer opportunities for long-term professional and economic advancement.
Programming will include:
An industry-focused presentation;
Interactive question-and-answer opportunities;
Speed networking with industry professionals;
Career pathway information;
Workforce and educational resources; and
Direct professional connections.
The initiative is particularly focused on high school, college, and trade school students, as well as adults interested in entering or transitioning into skilled-trade and design-related careers.
Meet industry professionals. Explore career pathways. Build your future.
This initiative reflects the Department's broader workforce development strategy of connecting residents with industries experiencing workforce demand while helping employers build stronger talent pipelines.
CONCLUSION
July 2026 demonstrated continued and measurable momentum for economic development in Greenacres. From advancing hotel and redevelopment opportunities along Lake Worth Road to successfully hosting an international consular initiative, expanding entrepreneurial assistance, strengthening business partnerships, and developing new workforce pathways, the Department continues moving strategic initiatives from relationships to opportunities and from opportunities to results.
These accomplishments demonstrate the value of collaboration among local government, businesses, educational institutions, nonprofit organizations, regional partners, and international stakeholders.
As Greenacres celebrates its Centennial Year, the Economic Development Department remains focused on building upon this momentum by attracting quality investment, supporting existing businesses, developing the City's future workforce, and creating opportunities that strengthen economic prosperity and quality of life.

description:
In 2023, the Florida Legislature authorized municipalities to install speed detection systems to enforce school zone speed limits. Following this legislative change, the City of Greenacres evaluated traffic data indicating significant speeding violations within City school zones. In 2023 alone, 707 speeding citations and 247 written warnings were issued within Greenacres school zones.
To enhance public safety and protect children traveling to and from school, the City Council directed staff to implement a School Zone Speed Enforcement Program using automated speed detection systems. Ordinance No. 2024-30 established the framework for this program, including the authority to contract with qualified vendors.
On May 19, 2025, City Council approved Resolution No. 2025-26 authorizing execution of a piggyback agreement with American Traffic Solutions, Inc. d/b/a Verra Mobility, utilizing the competitively awarded contract between the City of Tampa and Verra Mobility. The agreement provides for the installation, operation, and management of school zone speed camera enforcement services under the terms and rates outlined in Tampa’s Master Agreement.
On December 1, 2025, City Council approved Resolution No. 2025-58 authorizing execution of the First Amendment to the Agreement with Verra Mobility to add four (4) beacon lights to the City’s school zones.
The City has since been informed that the City of Tampa terminated its agreement with Verra Mobility. Because the City’s existing Piggyback Agreement is tied to the Tampa Agreement, the termination of the Tampa Agreement triggered the termination provision in the City’s Piggyback Agreement.
The City’s school zone speed camera system is currently in the implementation and installation phase. Verra Mobility has begun installation activities and has incurred equipment and implementation costs. If the City does not proceed with the program at this stage, the City may be responsible for reimbursing certain installed equipment costs in accordance with the existing agreement.

The provision states:
(8)(a) Each county and municipality shall apply to the FDEP for authorization of at least one debris management site as described in subsection (2) and shall annually seek pre-authorization for any previously approved debris management sites, as allowed by the department.
(b) A municipality may jointly apply for authorization of a debris management site with a county or at least one adjacent municipality, if the parties develop and approve a memorandum of understanding. Such memorandum must clearly outline the capacity of the debris management site and location of the site relative to each party. The memorandum of understanding must be approved annually as part of the preauthorization process described in paragraph (a).

description: City Code, Charter, Article II, Mayor, Section 2, Deputy Mayor states:The City Council shall designate one (1) of its members as Deputy Mayor, who shall serve in such capacity at the pleasure of the Council. The Deputy Mayor shall perform all the mayoral duties during the absence or disability of the Mayor. In the event of the simultaneous absence of the Mayor and Deputy Mayor at a City Council meeting, and with the existence of a quorum, the Councilmembers present at such meeting shall elect one (1) of its members to preside over the meeting. That presiding Councilmember shall retain all voting powers during the duration of said meeting. Due to the rescinding of Council Policy 12 in 2016, there are no provisions regarding term of appointment or criteria to be eligible to serve as Deputy Mayor.
title: Appointment of Deputy Mayor. - Mayor Chuck Shaw.
